question: A person sells a table at a 7% profit. If he had sold it for ₹1,280 more, then his profit would have been 17%. Find the cost price of the table.
solution:
[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__

Extra profit = 17% − 7% = 10%

10% of CP = 1280

⇒ CP = 1280 ÷ 10 × 100

⇒ CP = 12800

**∴ Answer = ₹12800**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

**Given:**

Profit₁ = 7%, Profit₂ = 17%, Difference in SP = 1280

**Formula used:**

SP = CP × (1 + Profit/100)

**Calculation:**

⇒ Let CP = x

⇒ SP₁ = 1.07x

⇒ SP₂ = 1.17x

⇒ Difference = 1.17x − 1.07x

⇒ 0.10x = 1280

⇒ x = 1280 ÷ 0.10

⇒ x = 12800

**∴ The correct answer is ₹12800.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

Profit Formula

SP = CP × (1 + Profit/100)

Shortcut Concept

Difference in profit % directly applies on CP

Percentage Conversion

10% = 0.10

Quick Check

7% of 12800 = 896, SP = 13696; 17% = 2176, SP = 14976; Difference = 1280 ✔
